text:
anoa: Heads-up — trying to run the @redwood-js SDK in Cloudflare Workers and hitting issues around Node builtins (Buffer, process.env) and CJS/ESM interop. wrangler dev crashes on import.
michael: ugh, classic. Is this the published bundle or your local dev build?
anoa: published 1.4.2 distro. Importing like `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` then immediately `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'byteLength')` coming from code that expects Buffer.
jenna: Cloudflare has globalThis.crypto.subtle and atob/btoa, but no Buffer. We should avoid Buffer in the runtime. Any stack trace?
anoa: stack points at `lib/utils/encoding.js` inside package. It does `Buffer.from(str)` in a helper. Quick hack in worker: `globalThis.Buffer = globalThis.Buffer || { from: s => Uint8Array.from(atob(s), c=>c.charCodeAt(0)) }` — works but gross.
ryan: We shouldn't recommend that hack. SDK should ship a small browser/worker-friendly encoding helper and package.json exports that point to a `dist/esm/worker.js` build.
deploy-bot: :info: release 1.4.3 published (chore: add worker build)
michael: Also CJS/ESM interop — some bundlers (esbuild w/target=node) still try to load `main` which points to cjs, and wrangler uses ESM. If package.json has both `main` and `module`/`exports` entries incorrectly gated, consumers get the wrong flavor.
jenna: For TS consumers on workers, add `typings: dist/esm/index.d.ts` and set `exports` with conditional exports: {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js","worker":"./dist/worker/index.js"} — that helps modern bundlers pick the right file.
anoa: Would adding a top-level `browser` field help older bundlers? Some customers still report rollups picking node shims that bloat bundles.
ryan: Yes, `browser` helps but it's brittle. Prefer explicit worker/browser build and document `import 'redwood-inference/worker'` for wrangler dev. Also recommend `esbuild --platform=browser` or `tsup --target=es2020 --format=esm`.
michael: Typings: folks on teams hit TS errors when using `esModuleInterop: false`. Our generated d.ts uses `export =` in cjs paths and `export default` in esm which confuses `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`. Recommend docs: set `esModuleInterop: true` or import `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` as fallback.
jenna: On retries/auth — Workers' fetch has slightly different signal/cancellation semantics. The SDK retry wrapper should avoid node AbortController shims and rely on the web AbortController. Tests blew up when we used `node-abort-controller`.
anoa: TL;DR: action items: 1) remove Buffer/fs usage or guard with web-friendly fallbacks, 2) publish explicit worker/esm/cjs builds and conditional exports, 3) add a short 'Cloudflare Workers' note in the README with recommended bundler flags and TS settings, 4) tweak retry/auth to use web AbortController.
ryan: I'll open a draft PR to add a `dist/worker` entry, small `isomorphic-encoding` helper, and docs. Assigning to @michael for packaging changes.
michael: on it — will also add a small test matrix run with `wrangler dev` in CI (smoke only) so we catch regressions.
devex-bot: :white_check_mark: created issue #1428 for worker compatibility and linked PR 2157.
anoa: Awesome — thanks. If we can get a patch release that avoids injecting Buffer shims into prod code, that'll save a lot of customer weirdness. :thumbsup:
